messages.subject: R workshop Sept 12-15
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!
In the week before the fall quarter begins, UC Davis Datalab is running a free four-day workshop for learning R; plus reproducible research tools like shell scripting, Git, and Github. The workshop runs 10am-3pm (with a break for lunch) on 9/12-9/15 (Monday - Thursday).

Please consider signing up, or share this notice with anyone you know who might be interested. Thanks!
-Wesley

Here is a signup link:
https://registration.genomecenter.ucdavis.edu/events/IntroToCollaborativeReproducibleResearchPracticesR/apply/

And here is a bit more information:
https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/introduction-to-collaborative-and-reproducible-research-practices-with-r-part-1-of-4/

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Sharing in case there are any people out there looking for (or know someone looking for) a post-doc with strong statistical and modeling skills. Feel free to share.

Best,
Ann

Sent: Wednesday, August 31, 2022 8:25 AM
To: Alexander L Forrest <alfo...@ucdavis.edu>; S Geoffrey Schladow <gsch...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: two new postdocs

Alex and Geoff,

I hope you are both doing well! We have two postdoc positions that are formally opening next week. In the meantime, I am hoping to identify some candidates.

Project descriptions are given in the ideal candidate statements below. Please let me know if you think of any students who would be interested.

Postdoc 1 Ideal Candidate Statement

The ideal candidate will possess a PhD in engineering, mathematics, statistics, computational biology, epidemiology, biology, bioinformatics, or computer science. The ideal candidate need not necessarily have direct experience with water treatment or water-related data, but will demonstrate experience with advanced applied statistical methods and possess the ability to construct statistical models from scratch while learning new application areas. This position is funded by a grant that focuses on constructing, evaluating, and analyzing a dynamic quantitative microbial risk assessment for the Las Vegas Valley. The project also involves constructing a machine learning model to project recycled water contribution in surface water.

Postdoc 2 Ideal Candidate Statement

The ideal candidate will possess a PhD in engineering, mathematics, statistics, computational biology, or computer science. The ideal candidate will have demonstrated experience with mathematical modeling with strong proficiency in R, Python, and/or MATLAB and an ability to learn new application areas. The candidate need not have direct experience with water treatment or water-related models. This position is funded by a grant that focuses on robust updates to the existing hydrodynamic and water quality model for Lake Mead, which is implemented in AEM3D. The ideal candidate will be responsible for learning, updating, running, and postprocessing the Lake Mead Model.

Thank you,

Deena Hannoun, Ph.D.

Limnology Modeling Project Manager, Southern Nevada Water Authority

deena....@snwa.com

(702) 856-5041
